function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide to the most popular “startup‑stat” APIs that let you pull data on companies, funding rounds, investors, exits, and more.  
I’ve grouped them by provider, listed the key endpoints, and shown a minimal example (Python‑style `requests_get` call) so you can copy‑paste and test right away.  

> **Tip** – Most of these services require an API key or OAuth token.  
> If you don’t already have one, sign up for a free tier or a trial; the examples below use a placeholder (`YOUR_API_KEY`) that you’ll replace with your own key.

---

## 1. Crunchbase API (v3.1)

Crunchbase is the industry standard for startup data.  
The free tier allows ~200 requests/month (good for prototyping).

| Endpoint | What it returns | Example query |
|----------|-----------------|---------------|
| `/organizations` | List of companies (search by name, domain, etc.) | `?name=Stripe` |
| `/organizations/{id}` | Detailed company profile | `/organizations/stripe` |
| `/organizations/{id}/funding_rounds` | Funding rounds for a company | `/organizations/stripe/funding_rounds` |
| `/investors` | List of investors | `?name=Sequoia` |
| `/investments` | Investment deals | `?organization=Stripe` |

### Sample call – get a company profile

```python
from functions import requests_get

response = requests_get({
    "url": "https://api.crunchbase.com/v3.1/organizations/stripe",
    "headers": {"Accept": "application/json"},
    "params": {"user_key": "YOUR_API_KEY"}
})
print(response)
```

> **Response snippet**  
> ```json
> {
>   "data": {
>     "organization": {
>       "name": "Stripe",
>       "homepage_url": "https://stripe.com",
>       "founded_on": "2010-06-14",
>       "total_funding_amount": 1100000000,
>       ...
>     }
>   }
> }
> ```

---

## 2. AngelList API (GraphQL)

AngelList offers a GraphQL endpoint that’s very flexible.  
Free tier: 10 k requests/month.

| Query | What it returns |
|-------|-----------------|
| `companies` | List of companies (filter by name, location, etc.) |
| `company(id)` | Detailed company data |
| `investments` | Investment deals |

### Sample GraphQL query – list companies named “Stripe”

```python
from functions import requests_get

query = """
{
  companies(query: "Stripe", page: 1, per_page: 5) {
    nodes {
      id
      name
      website
      founded_at
      funding_rounds {
        total_amount
        currency
      }
    }
  }
}
"""

response = requests_get({
    "url": "https://api.angel.co/1/graphql",
    "headers": {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "Accept": "application/json",
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
    },
    "params": {"query": query}
})
print(response)
```

> **Response snippet**  
> ```json
> {
>   "data": {
>     "companies": {
>       "nodes": [
>         {
>           "id": "12345",
>           "name": "Stripe",
>           "website": "https://stripe.com",
>           "founded_at": "2010-06-14",
>           "funding_rounds": [
>             {"total_amount": 1100000000, "currency": "USD"}
>           ]
>         }
>       ]
>     }
>   }
> }
> ```

---

## 3. PitchBook API (via Data Axle)

PitchBook is a premium source; they offer a limited free trial.  
Endpoints are RESTful and return JSON.

| Endpoint | What it returns |
|----------|-----------------|
| `/companies` | Company search |
| `/funding_rounds` | Funding round data |
| `/investors` | Investor profiles |

> **Note** – PitchBook requires a signed contract; the free trial is usually 30 days.

---

## 4. CB Insights API (via Data Axle)

CB Insights provides a “Company Intelligence” API.  
Free tier: 500 requests/month.

| Endpoint | What it returns |
|----------|-----------------|
| `/companies` | Company search |
| `/funding_rounds` | Funding round data |
| `/acquisitions` | M&A activity |

---

## 5. Open Data Sources

If you’re looking for completely free data (no auth), consider:

| Source | Data |
|--------|------|
| **Crunchbase Open Data** (CSV) | Downloadable CSVs of companies, funding, etc. |
| **AngelList Public Data** | GitHub repo with scraped company data |
| **Data.gov** | Startup datasets (e.g., Small Business Administration) |

These are static files; you’ll need to load them into your own database or use a CSV‑to‑JSON converter.

---

## 6. Quick‑Start Checklist

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| 1 | Sign up for a free account on Crunchbase, AngelList, or CB Insights. |
| 2 | Grab your API key / OAuth token. |
| 3 | Pick the endpoint that matches the data you need (company, funding, investor). |
| 4 | Use the sample code above, replacing `YOUR_API_KEY` or `YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN`. |
| 5 | Handle pagination (`page`, `per_page`) if you need more than the default limit. |
| 6 | Store the JSON in your database or cache for later analysis. |

---

## 7. Common Pitfalls & Tips

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Rate limits** | Cache responses; use exponential back‑off. |
| **Missing fields** | Some fields are optional; check for `null` before accessing. |
| **Auth errors** | Verify that the key is active and has the right scopes. |
| **Large payloads** | Use `stream=True` in `requests_get` if you’re downloading huge CSVs. |
| **Data freshness** | Crunchbase updates daily; AngelList updates weekly. |

---

### Final Thought

Pick the provider that best matches your budget and data needs.  
For a quick prototype, the Crunchbase free tier or AngelList GraphQL API are usually enough.  
If you need deeper, enterprise‑grade data, consider PitchBook or CB Insights (they’ll require a paid plan).

Happy data hunting! 🚀
